references.text: The parallel passage in Mark tells that Jesus went around throughout Galilee and preached in their synagogues. Mark 1:39 is the direct parallel to Luke 4:44.
Matthew describes how Jesus went around throughout Galilee, teaching in their synagogues and preaching the gospel of the kingdom – a parallel to Jesus' preaching journey in the synagogues.

Earlier in the same chapter it is told that Jesus returned to Galilee in the power of the Spirit and taught in the synagogues there. This forms the background for his continued preaching activity in verse 44.

The preceding verses explain that the crowd wanted to keep Jesus, but he said he must preach the kingdom of God also to the other cities, for that is why he was sent. Verse 44 is the direct follow-up to this statement.
Jesus went around in all the towns and villages, teaching in the synagogues, preaching the gospel and healing – this shows the same pattern of preaching in the synagogues as in Luke 4:44.
Jesus himself says that he has always taught in synagogues and in the temple, where all the Jews gather. This confirms the pattern we see in Luke 4:44.
Peter's speech in Acts summarizes Jesus' ministry, which began in Galilee after the baptism John preached – a summary of the preaching service described in Luke 4:44.
Luke describes again that Jesus went from city to city and from village to village, preaching the gospel of the kingdom of God. This continues the pattern from Luke 4:44.
